He reads the three samidhs as Agni's three bodies in earthly, lightning and solar form (pārthiva-vaidyuta-sūrya-rūpāḥ tanūḥ), the earthly one placed in the world of mortals (martye martyaloke adadhuḥ), the other two gone to the mid-air, and then offers the alternative (athavā) of the three fuel sticks, two āghāra and one anūyāja; Wilson's note on the verse reports both readings. The paraphrase carries nothing beyond these words. Verse: verse.js ok, ref Rig Veda 3.2.9, at [235,9], a text unit. Plain sense: Vaisvanara is 3.2.1 and the great High Priest of Gods is 3.2.8, so the context clause is the hymn's own; 'threefold fire' names the verse's three splendours of Agni without borrowing its words.
